items.title: From candle hue to displacement and density gradient
items.subject: Quantitative RSD
items.description: A synchronized three-panel view of the hue-extracted candle, calibrated focal-plane displacement, and estimated path-averaged air-equivalent density gradient. Calibration uses 0.05 mm translation per image and the unlit-candle background. The mirror focal length is 1500 mm; the effective optical path is estimated as 20 mm.
items.note: The gradient magnitude depends on the estimated path length and air Gladstone–Dale constant. Saturated and out-of-calibration pixels are masked; color scales stay fixed. This is not an Abel reconstruction. Every fourth source frame · 30 fps playback; acquisition timing unconfirmed

context.title: Reading schlieren images
context.text: Schlieren imaging responds to refractive-index gradients. The image sequences here use stated presentation rates; acquisition frame rates have not been confirmed, so their playback is not a physical time scale. The calibrated candle result uses a confirmed 1500 mm focal length and an estimated 20 mm optical path. Its density gradient is a path-averaged air-equivalent estimate, with ambiguous and out-of-range hues masked. A separate Abel reconstruction would require an image length scale and an axisymmetry assessment.
